# storagekit (@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit)

> Unified TypeScript file management across Local filesystem, AWS S3, MinIO, Azure Blob Storage, Oracle OCI Object Storage and RustFS. One common API for common operations, with strongly-typed **provider-native options** preserved under a `native` key instead of being flattened to a lowest common denominator. Runs on Node.js >= 20, Bun >= 1.1 and Deno >= 2 (all smoke-tested in CI). Dual ESM/CJS with full TypeScript declarations. Custom drivers can be registered against the same API.

## Install

```bash
npm install @mohamedhabibwork/storagekit
# Provider SDKs are optional peer dependencies — install only what you use:
# S3 / RustFS: npm i @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/lib-storage @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner
# MinIO:       npm i minio
# Azure:       npm i @azure/storage-blob
# Oracle:      npm i oci-common oci-objectstorage
# Local:       no extra dependency (Node built-ins only)
```

**Entrypoints** (import only what you use; the root entry bundles no cloud SDK):
`@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit` (core + factory + manager + copyBetween + upload intake),
`.../local`, `.../s3`, `.../minio`, `.../azure`, `.../oracle`, `.../rustfs`
(each also exports `createXxxStorage`), `.../testing` (driver contract suite),
`.../uploads` (upload intake helpers), `.../adapters/express`,
`.../adapters/fastify`, `.../adapters/formidable` (framework upload adapters).

Loading a driver without its SDK installed throws `StorageInvalidConfigError`
with the exact `npm install` command — never a module-not-found crash.

## Core rule

Common options are normalized and identical on every provider. Anything
provider-specific goes in `native`, strongly typed by the configured storage
type: `Storage<'s3'>` accepts real AWS fields (`StorageClass`,
`ServerSideEncryption`, `ACL`, …) while `Storage<'azure'>` accepts Azure
fields (`tier`, `conditions`, `tags`, …) and REJECTS AWS fields at compile
time. `native` is merged last and overrides common equivalents.

## Creating a storage (async)

```ts
import { createStorage } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit';

// Returns Promise<Storage<'s3'>> — the type parameter is inferred from `type`
const s3 = await createStorage({
  type: 's3',                    // 'local' | 's3' | 'minio' | 'azure' | 'oracle'
  bucket: 'uploads',
  region: 'eu-central-1',
});
```

Required config per type:
- `local`: `root` (required); optional `baseUrl` (powers `getUrl()`), `prefix`, `permissions`, `createDirectories`, `followSymlinks`
- `s3`: `bucket`; optional `region`, `endpoint`, `credentials`, `forcePathStyle`, `prefix`, `publicUrlBase`, `client` (inject S3Client), `clientOptions`
- `minio`: `bucket`, `endPoint`; optional `port`, `useSSL`, `accessKey`, `secretKey`, `region`, `prefix`, `publicUrlBase`, `client`, `clientOptions`
- `azure`: `container` + ONE auth route: `connectionString` | `accountUrl` (+ `credential`: shared key or TokenCredential) | `serviceClient` | `containerClient`; optional `prefix`, `publicUrlBase`
- `oracle`: `namespaceName`, `bucketName`; optional `region`, `prefix`, `publicUrlBase`, `auth` (`{type:'config-file'|'instance-principals'|'resource-principals'|'provider'}`), `authProvider`, `client`, `clientOptions`
- `rustfs`: `bucket` + `endpoint` (required); optional `region` (default `us-east-1`), `credentials`, `forcePathStyle` (default `true`), `prefix`, `publicUrlBase`, `client`, `clientOptions`. RustFS is S3-compatible but ships no first-party JS SDK — `native()` returns `S3Client` and every `native` option accepts the AWS SDK input fields.

All providers accept an optional `prefix` (e.g. `'production/'`): every
operation transparently stores/lists under that prefix and strips it from
results.

Second factory argument (all optional):
`{ hooks, onOperation, detectContentType }`. `detectContentType` defaults to
true and is a lightweight extension→MIME map; pass `contentType` explicitly
when it matters.

## Upload

```ts
// body: string | Buffer | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | Blob | Node Readable
await storage.upload('users/1/avatar.jpg', buffer, {
  contentType: 'image/jpeg',          // normalized
  metadata: { userId: '100' },        // normalized
  cacheControl: 'public,max-age=31536000',
  contentDisposition: '…', contentEncoding: '…',
  overwrite: false,                   // default true; false = HEAD check + StorageConflictError
  signal: controller.signal,          // cancellation everywhere
  multipart: { partSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024, concurrency: 4 },
  native: { StorageClass: 'INTELLIGENT_TIERING' },   // provider-native, typed
});
// → { path, size?, etag?, versionId?, url?, provider, native? }
```

Streams are never buffered into memory. Multipart mapping: S3 → `@aws-sdk/lib-storage`
(`partSize`, `concurrency` → `queueSize`); Azure → `uploadStream(bufferSize, maxConcurrency)`;
Oracle → native multipart API (partSize floored at 1 MiB, default 64 MiB);
MinIO → its internal multipart (size unknown); local → plain stream write.

Provider-native field examples:
- S3: `StorageClass`, `ServerSideEncryption: 'aws:kms'`, `SSEKMSKeyId`, `ACL`, `Tagging`
- Azure: `tier: 'Cool'`, `conditions`, `tags`, `blobHTTPHeaders`
- MinIO: `metaData: { … }` (extra x-amz-meta bag)
- Oracle: `storageTier: 'Archive'`, `ifMatch`, `opcMeta`, `opcChecksumAlgorithm`
- Local: `mode: 0o600`

## Framework uploads (multer, @fastify/multipart, formidable, web File)

```ts
// Core intake — works with ANY upload middleware. Import from 'storagekit/uploads'
// (also re-exported from the root entry).
import { saveUpload, sanitizeFilename, randomKey } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit/uploads';
const saved = await saveUpload(storage, {
  body: file.stream,              // stream | Buffer | Blob
  fieldname: file.fieldname,
  originalName: file.originalname, // untrusted: used only for key EXTENSION + metadata
  mimeType: file.mimetype,
}, { directory: 'uploads' });      // → uploads/<uuid>.<ext from original name>
// saved: { key, originalName?, mimeType?, result }  (result = UploadResult)
// Auto metadata: originalname/fieldname/mimetype (merge via `metadata: {...}`,
// disable with `metadata: false`). `key` accepts a string or async resolver —
// both traversal-checked. `native`, `signal`, `overwrite`, `contentType` pass through.

// Express / NestJS / koa-multer — multer storage engine ('storagekit/adapters/express'):
import multer from 'multer';
import { createMulterStorage } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit/adapters/express';
const upload = multer({ storage: createMulterStorage(storage, { directory: 'uploads' }) });
app.post('/u', upload.single('avatar'), (req, res) =>
  res.json({ key: req.file!.key, etag: req.file!.etag, storagekit: req.file!.storagekit }));
// NestJS: FileInterceptor('avatar', { storage: createMulterStorage(storage) })
// Request aborted / handler error → stored object is deleted (_removeFile).

// Fastify 4/5 ('storagekit/adapters/fastify'):
import { saveFastifyFile } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit/adapters/fastify';
app.post('/u', async (req) => {
  const part = await req.file();
  return saveFastifyFile(storage, part!, { directory: 'uploads' }); // consumes the stream
});

// Hono / Next.js / Remix / Nuxt / Elysia / Bun.serve / Deno.serve — web File:
import { saveWebFile } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit/uploads';
const saved = await saveWebFile(storage, fileFromFormData, { directory: 'uploads' });

// formidable v2/v3 ('storagekit/adapters/formidable'):
import { saveFormidableFile } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit/adapters/formidable';
const saved = await saveFormidableFile(storage, files.file, { directory: 'uploads' });
// Koa (@koa/multer) uses the same multer engine; busboy / GraphQL Upload →
// wrap the part into UploadFileInput and call saveUpload(). Serve files back
// via getUrl() (local needs baseUrl), getSignedUrl() (Oracle: PARs, not
// presigned), or download() + stream. Validate client MIME/size yourself
// (multer fileFilter + limits run before the engine).
```

Adapters import NOTHING from the frameworks (structural types only) — every
framework package stays an optional peer. Client filenames never control the
key stem: `randomKey()` uses a UUID; `sanitizeFilename()` keeps only a safe
basename/extension.

## Download

```ts
const dl = await storage.download('docs/report.pdf', {
  versionId: '…',                     // where the provider supports it
  range: { offset: 100, length: 50 }, // byte range where supported
  signal,
});
dl.stream            // Node Readable — pipe it somewhere
dl.contentType; dl.contentLength; dl.etag; dl.lastModified; dl.metadata; dl.versionId
await dl.buffer(); await dl.text(); await dl.json<MyType>();
```

Always consume the stream (or call `.buffer()/.text()/.json()`). If you abort,
`stream.destroy()` it.

## Exists / stat / delete

```ts
await storage.exists('a.txt');                    // HEAD-based, never downloads
const st = await storage.stat('a.txt');           // { path, size, contentType?, etag?, lastModified?, metadata?, versionId?, provider }
await storage.delete('a.txt');                    // IDEMPOTENT: deleting a missing object is a no-op
await storage.deleteMany(['a', 'b', 'c']);        // → { deleted: string[], failed: [{ path, error }] }
```

Missing file: `download`/`stat` throw `StorageNotFoundError`; `delete`/`deleteMany`
succeed silently. `exists` returns false.

## List / iterate

```ts
// default (recursive: false) = ONE level deep, like S3 with delimiter
const page = await storage.list({ prefix: 'users/100/', limit: 100, cursor });
page.files;        // StorageFile[]: { path, size?, etag?, lastModified?, metadata? }
page.directories;  // ['users/100/sub/'] — trailing slash, one level
page.cursor;       // opaque token — pass back as { cursor } verbatim
page.hasMore;

// recursive flat scan (all files under prefix, directories empty)
await storage.list({ prefix: 'uploads/', recursive: true, limit: 1000 });

// async iteration — pagination handled for you, yields files only
for await (const file of storage.iterate('uploads/')) { file.path; }
```

`limit` defaults to 1000 and bounds entries per page (files + directories).
Cursors are opaque driver-specific tokens: only round-trip them, never parse
or persist across config changes.

## Copy / move / cross-provider copy

```ts
await storage.copy('temp/a.jpg', 'images/a.jpg');   // server-side copy
await storage.move('temp/a.pdf', 'docs/a.pdf');     // copy + delete (rename on local)

import { copyBetween } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit';
await copyBetween(srcStorage, 'docs/f.pdf', dstStorage, 'archive/f.pdf', {
  concurrency: 4, onProgress: (bytes, total) => {},
});
```

`copy` streams server-to-server within a provider. Cross-provider always
streams through the process (never fully buffered) — use `copyBetween`.

## URLs

```ts
await storage.getUrl('images/logo.png');      // unsigned; no network call
await storage.getSignedUrl('private.pdf', { expiresIn: 3600, action: 'read' }); // 'read' | 'write' | 'delete'
```

`expiresIn` is seconds, default 3600, hard-capped at 604800 (7 days) — out of
range throws. S3/MinIO/RustFS: presigned; Azure: SAS via shared key / connection
string (TokenCredential needs user-delegation via `nativeRequest`); local:
throws `StorageUnsupportedOperationError` (serve through your app); Oracle:
throws — it has no presigned URLs. `createOracleStorage()` (subpath import)
adds `createPreauthenticatedRequest()` for Oracle PARs, whose lifecycle is
persistent server-side and fundamentally different from presigned URLs.

## Escaping the abstraction

```ts
const client = storage.native();            // S3Client | ContainerClient | Minio.Client | ObjectStorageClient | {root, resolve}
await storage.nativeRequest((c) => c.anySdkCall());   // typed native client
storage.capabilities();                     // { signedUrls, multipartUpload, serverSideCopy, versioning, metadata, directories, bulkDelete }
```

Check `capabilities()` instead of assuming a feature exists; unsupported
features throw `StorageUnsupportedOperationError` rather than being silently
emulated.

## Errors

```ts
import { StorageNotFoundError, isStorageError } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit';
try { await storage.download(p); } catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof StorageNotFoundError) { /* missing */ }
  e.provider;  e.operation;  e.path;  e.code;  e.cause;  // original SDK error
}
```

Classes: `StorageError` (base), `StorageNotFoundError`,
`StoragePermissionError`, `StorageConflictError`, `StorageInvalidConfigError`,
`StorageNetworkError`, `StorageQuotaError`,
`StorageUnsupportedOperationError`, `StorageInvalidPathError`. Use
`isStorageError(e)` when errors may cross entrypoint copies. Provider errors
are preserved on `cause` and never leak credentials into messages.

## Multiple disks / manager

```ts
const disks = createStorageManager({ default: 'uploads', disks: {
  uploads: { type: 's3', bucket: 'uploads' },
  temp: { type: 'local', root: './tmp' },
}});
await disks.disk('uploads').upload('a.txt', 'x');   // typed per disk config
await disks.defaultDisk();
```

## Hooks & events

```ts
const storage = await createStorage(config, {
  hooks: { beforeUpload, afterUpload, uploadError, beforeDownload,
           afterDownload, downloadError, beforeDelete, afterDelete, deleteError },
  onOperation: (e) => e.provider && e.duration && e.success,
});
const off = storage.on('operation', (e) => {}); off();
// event: { provider, operation, path?, duration, success, error? }
```

Hook contexts are sanitized: credentials and signed URLs never appear.
Hook errors in `beforeX` abort nothing silently — `beforeX` errors propagate;
`xxxError` hooks never mask the original failure.

## Key semantics (do not get these wrong)

- Keys always use `/`. Input is normalized: backslashes, duplicate slashes,
  leading/trailing slashes, `.` segments. `..` traversal throws
  `StorageInvalidPathError`; local paths can never escape the configured root.
- `overwrite` defaults to true everywhere; `overwrite: false` costs one extra
  metadata round-trip.
- Deleting missing objects is a no-op on every provider (idempotent).
- `native` overrides common options when both set the same field.
- Everything network-bound accepts `signal`.
- Export maps are dual ESM/CJS with full TypeScript declarations; types work
  with `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` / `'node16'`.

## Best practices

1. Import provider subpaths (`.../s3`) in bundled apps so only one SDK ships.
2. `await createStorage(...)` — the factory loads the SDK and builds clients.
3. Stream large files; never `readFile` then upload the buffer.
4. Set `contentType` explicitly for user-facing correctness; extension
   detection is a convenience, not a guarantee.
5. Pass `signal` on long transfers and wire it to request timeouts.
6. Scan big buckets with `iterate()` (or `list({recursive:true})` paging), not
   unpaginated `list()`.
7. Round-trip `cursor` opaquely; don't persist cursors across restarts of a
   changed config.
8. Same-provider copies: `storage.copy()` (server-side). Different providers:
   `copyBetween()`.
9. Reach for `native()` / `nativeRequest()` for unsupported SDK features
   instead of bypassing the package.
10. Catch specific error subclasses; log `e.cause` for provider-side detail.
11. For local `getUrl()`, configure `baseUrl` (or use `native: { fileUrl: true }`).
12. Versioning differs per provider: `versionId` is normalized on
   download/stat/delete, but semantics (S3 vs Azure vs OCI) are not identical —
   don't assume one behavior.

## Custom drivers

Implement `StorageDriver<T>` (exported), register it, then create storages
with that type string. Builtin type names cannot be overridden; duplicate
registrations throw `StorageInvalidConfigError`.

```ts
import { registerStorageDriver, defineDriver, type StorageDriver } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit';

const driver: StorageDriver<'memory'> = defineDriver({
  type: 'memory',
  upload(path, body, options) { /* returns { path, size?, etag?, versionId?, url?, provider } */ },
  download(path) { /* returns { stream, contentType?, contentLength?, buffer(), text(), json() } */ },
  delete(path) {},                                    // idempotent, like builtins
  deleteMany(paths, options) { /* { deleted, failed } */ },
  exists(path) { /* HEAD-style check */ },
  stat(path) { /* FileStat */ },
  list(options) { /* { files, directories (trailing '/'), cursor, hasMore } — one level unless options.recursive */ },
  copy(source, destination, options) {},
  move(source, destination, options) {},              // copy + delete
  getUrl(path) { /* unsigned URL or throw StorageUnsupportedOperationError */ },
  getSignedUrl(path, options) { /* or throw unsupported */ },
  native() { return client; },
  nativeRequest(fn) { return fn(native()); },
  capabilities() { return { signedUrls: false, multipartUpload: true, serverSideCopy: true, versioning: false, metadata: true, directories: false, bulkDelete: false }; },
});

registerStorageDriver('memory', (config, runtime) => driver);
const storage = await createStorage({ type: 'memory', /* custom fields */ });
```

Custom types get `unknown` native slots (`MapValueFor` fallback). Optional
async `ready()` on the driver is awaited by the factory. The registry is
shared process-wide (globalThis symbol), visible across entrypoints.
Missing methods (missing `type` string / non-function `upload`/`download`)
are rejected at registration/use with `StorageInvalidConfigError`.

## Testing custom drivers

```ts
import { defineDriverContractTests } from '@mohamedhabibwork/storagekit/testing';
defineDriverContractTests({ name: 'mine', createStorage: () => make(), capabilities: { signedUrls: true } });
```

## Runtime support

- Node.js >= 20 (primary; CI on 20/22), Bun >= 1.1, Deno >= 2 (npm compat).
- Every build runs `scripts/runtime-smoke.mjs` on all three runtimes in CI:
  local driver streams/listings/errors + custom-driver registry.
- Cloud SDKs are regular npm packages and work on all three; the local
  driver uses only `node:` built-ins that all three runtimes implement.
